experiment: RSNN_TRSF (transformer + dihedral) vs GET on PDBbind-Benchmark identity30

protocol.note: GET native recipe (20 epochs); RSNN up to 500 epochs, early stop patience 50, standardized target.

best_config.name: dropout0.1
best_config.why: Best transformer variant: 3-seed Pearson 0.5847 -- statistically indistinguishable from GET (0.5887); beats GET on Spearman & MAE. dropout is the lever that closes the ~6% gap of the naive rope/no-dropout config.

verdict: STATISTICAL PARITY. At equal parameter budget, RSNN_TRSF with dropout 0.1 matches the equivariant GET (overlapping error bars on all 4 metrics; 2/4 each -- GET edges Pearson/RMSE, transformer edges Spearman/MAE). The gap is closed by regularization, not equivariance. 'Transformer BEATS GET' is NOT supported (single-seed artifact).

followups_running.VERDICT_param_bump: HURTS. 712k (0.5371 +/- 0.0042) is clearly below the 692k baseline (0.5847); tight, non-overlapping error bars. Extra capacity overfits the small 3.5k-complex dataset. KEEP h120/692k.
followups_running.VERDICT_bond_graph: LOSES + far noisier. Bond graph 0.5297 +/- 0.0529 vs 4.5A distance 0.5847: lower mean AND ~5x the variance (seeds 0.478-0.603). The dense geometric 4.5A graph (bonds + through-space contacts) gives more stable, informative ligand walks than the sparse chemical bond graph. The 4.5A DISTANCE GRAPH is the better, more reliable ligand connectivity for this affinity task.
followups_running.BEST_OVERALL: dropout0.1, h120 (692k), 4.5A distance ligand graph, all-atom protein order -> Pearson 0.5847 +/- 0.0119, statistical parity with GET (0.5887). No ablation improved on it.

protein_torsion_ordering_ablation.verdict: HURTS vs all-atom (0.5847): -0.036 Pearson, tight non-overlapping error bars, worse on all 4 metrics. Real phi/psi/omega+chi ordering fragments the ~29-residue pocket into ~59 hard-reset segments (spine fragments + chi paths + tails + N/CA repeats) and loses local-contact context. Same 692k params; single lever = protein token order. Keep protein_order=allatom.
